name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised no money
model.rationale: Garcia holds a D+17 district, has out-raised an opponent who has reported no fundraising, and markets price her around 94% to win. With no polls or expert ratings available, fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Garcia could narrow the expected margin, though a seat this blue is unlikely to become competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She enters with roughly $1 million raised this cycle plus outside support, while Republican Martha Fierro has reported no fundraising and no outside backing. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which put Garcia's chances near 94 percent.

The combination of incumbency, a heavily Democratic electorate, and a resource gap makes an upset very unlikely. The main uncertainty is simply how large the margin will be, since the seat's low profile means little polling exists to sharpen the estimate.
